title: The next big AI model is here
author: Jay Peters

recommendations.name: the rise of GEO
recommendations.blurb: This week, I’m reading about the rise of GEO , laughing at Kirby’s new shapes , acknowledging Google’s good dunk on Apple , thinking of the best Wordle puzzle I can make, wondering if I’ll ever see Microsoft’s Windows XP-themed Crocs out in the wild, following the progress of The Bluesky Dictionary…

recommendations.name: OpenAI’s GPT-5
recommendations.blurb: OpenAI’s next major AI model is finally out. The company promises it has “state-of-the-art performance” across many different types of work and is “significantly less likely to hallucinate” than its previous models. You can try it out right now in ChatGPT, even if you’re on the free plan.

recommendations.name: OpenAI’s GPT-OSS
recommendations.blurb: Ahead of GPT-5, OpenAI also made a splash with the release of GPT-OSS, its two new open-weight models that you can run on a laptop . Having the power of an OpenAI model, with the privacy of a local model, is perhaps an even more compelling option.

recommendations.name: Roku’s Howdy
recommendations.blurb: This new subscription service has “thousands of titles” available ad-free for $2.99 per month.

recommendations.name: TP-Link’s Wi-Fi 7 BE3600 Travel Router
recommendations.blurb: This Wi-Fi 7 travel router seems like it could save you some wireless connection hassles while on a big family trip. It works with up to 90 devices at once, which I’m guessing will be more than enough for most families.

recommendations.name: Camp Snap CS-8
recommendations.blurb: This camera looks a bit like a classic Super 8 film camera, and while it uses SD card storage, there’s no screen you can use to see what you’ve shot. That could be annoying, but I also think it could be really fun.

recommendations.name: Fortnite’s new Shock ‘N Awesome season
recommendations.blurb: The latest battle royale update adds bug infestations to the Fortnite island, but you can take them on as a Power Ranger. This seems like a season made for 90s kids , so I don’t think I’ll be able to resist checking this out.

recommendations.name: Is This Seat Taken?
recommendations.blurb: If you’re looking for something a little lower key, this chill new puzzle game that asks you to find the right seat for adorable little shapes is great. I’ve played the whole thing, and it’s delightful .

recommendations.name: The 2025 Tiny Awards nominations
recommendations.blurb: You have until September 1st to vote on one of 11 extremely cool websites to be Site of the Year. I haven’t decided on my pick, but I’m a big fan of Cloudgazing .

recommendations.name: Dungeon Crawler Carl
recommendations.blurb: I just binged the 7th novel of Dungeon Crawler Carl so fast it was silly. Incredibly fun reads that are somewhat hard to describe. Maybe like… Hunger Games meets video games? Light-hearted and eminently binge-able. Who isn’t into Donkey Kong Bananza right now?

recommendations.blurb: For the first time in a few years I’m playing around with some embedded programming platforms, specifically Arduino and the Pi Pico . It’s amazing that I can get a computer more powerful than the desktop I owned in high school for less than ten dollars.

recommendations.name: Lord of the Rings audiobook
recommendations.blurb: I’m deeply impressed by the Lord of the Rings audiobook by Andy Serkis. It’s insane how differently the characters sound (and how similar to movies).

recommendations.name: Inoreader
recommendations.blurb: This week I took control of my RSS reader by moving from Inoreader to a self-hosted Miniflux instance. It was actually super easy to get working, and it’s cool to be able to use different third-party native apps again. It feels like I’m back in the good ol’ Google Reader days again.

recommendations.name: Superman: The Animated Series
recommendations.blurb: I’ve been watching Superman: The Animated Series on HBO Max. I love how the series makes the most of its sci-fi premise, alongside compelling cinematography and stirring music. Highly recommend!

recommendations.name: This video from Julian O’Shea
recommendations.blurb: This video from Julian O’Shea about cars getting huge is extremely well done, and the part about pedestrian fatalities is legitimately moving. If you’re in need of lighter fare, CityNerd’s new video about the Vegas Loop being pathetically stupid is a great follow up piece.

recommendations.name: mostly-QWERTY layout
recommendations.blurb: I use a mostly-QWERTY layout , but have a ZSA Moonlander keyboard and have customized it to my programmer/game tastes. I can actually touch-type now with this keyboard. It folds up so well that I travel with it all the time, and it gets comments every time I use it.

recommendations.name: Apocalypse Hotel
recommendations.blurb: I’d like to recommend Apocalypse Hotel ! It’s a charming anime about a group of robots running a hotel long after humanity left the planet. It’s got a lovely bittersweet but optimistic mood to it as they wait patiently for humanity to return. And it’s quite funny as well.

recommendations.blurb: Thanks to everyone who wrote in their stories of alternate keyboard layouts. There’s a fair few Dvorak users out there, but I heard from a fellow Colemak typist and even a Norman user!
